highlights: MVP delivery moved forward with 2 of 3 tasks completed, including the routing stabilization pass and the inbox acknowledgement patch.
You recovered well after one interrupted prompt-review session and followed it with a completed focus block to refine reflection coach prompts.
Recovery signals improved by the end of the week: sleep increased from 330 to 405 minutes, audio stress settled, and video fatigue eased after a shorter day.
blockers: Recovery work lagged behind delivery work: the missed-call review is blocked and the sleep trend check has not yet been closed out as a task.
Meeting-heavy windows caused at least one interrupted work block and raised stress markers midweek.
Short sleep late in the sprint pulled energy down even while delivery stayed on track.
trends: Focus was strongest early in the week, dropped during interruption-heavy periods, then improved again when work was broken into smaller blocks.
Energy was the least stable signal this week; low sleep aligned with higher fatigue and lower focus later in the sprint.
Execution on product work outpaced recovery maintenance, suggesting delivery is easier to advance than wellbeing-related tasks right now.
nextSuggestions: Close the loop on MVP delivery by scheduling one clearly bounded session to finish the remaining prompt-review task.
Unblock the recovery goal by defining the next smallest step for the missed-call review and updating the sleep trend check based on the session you already completed.
Protect energy with shorter focus blocks and a planned recharge break after meeting-heavy windows, especially after nights with under 6 hours of sleep.
